proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the effective lag varies over the season (e.g., changes near peak), a fixed 2-week delay can misalign shoulders or peak timing.
proposals.rationale: Baseline consistent with prior best spec; directly targets the dominant error source (phase/lag between infections proxy and hospital admissions) while keeping dynamics parsimonious for short, high-peakiness series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May shift predicted peak too early and overfit early growth, degrading fit on decline/late-season weeks.
proposals.rationale: Tests slightly shorter infectious-to-hospitalization reporting/admission lag while retaining the same SEIR dynamics; useful if this age group’s admissions respond faster than the 2-week baseline.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May delay the peak excessively and underpredict early-season rise, especially in high-peakiness seasons.
proposals.rationale: Tests slightly longer lag to accommodate slower progression-to-admission or reporting delays; still minimal complexity and centered near the empirically favored neighborhood around 2 weeks.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Likely systematic phase error (peak timing mismatch) if admissions lag infections, leading to biased forecasts around the peak.
proposals.rationale: No-lag single-state observation as a control to detect whether the series is effectively contemporaneous with the infectious proxy; keeps structure minimal and avoids added compartments.
